summary.short: Establishes the scientific panel of independent experts in AI provided for under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and sets its selection, composition (no more than 60 experts), independence, transparency and procedures for supporting market surveillance, qualified alerts and information requests to general-purpose AI model providers. Binding and directly applicable; enters into force on the twentieth day after publication.
summary.long: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/454 establishes the scientific panel of independent experts in AI provided for under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and sets its rules. The Commission appoints experts following a public call for expression of interest, with no more than 60 experts, aiming for gender balance and geographic representation, and with at least four-fifths of experts from EU Member States or EEA EFTA states. Experts serve a two-year term, renewable. They must be independent of AI system and general-purpose AI model providers, file declarations of interest and commitment, and keep confidential information secret. The AI Office and the Joint Research Centre provide the secretariat, which must publish the names, CVs and declarations of experts, the rules of procedure and panel opinions, except where confidential business information or trade secrets would be disclosed. The panel can support Member States' market surveillance authorities on request, and issues qualified alerts to the AI Office by at least a simple majority of its members. The panel may ask the AI Office to request documentation or information from general-purpose AI model providers, subject to necessity, proportionality, trade secret protection and data security safeguards. The regulation is binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States, and enters into force on the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal.

notes: Text-internal points: (1) Art. 12 refers to thematic hearings under Art. 7(4), but they are provided for in Art. 7(5); Art. 7(4) concerns Commission evaluations under Art. 92(2) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. (2) Recital (13) cites the opinion of the 'Artificial Intelligence Committee', whereas the recitals and articles use the 'European Artificial Intelligence Board'; the text does not define the Committee. (3) The body appointing rapporteurs and contributors varies: the Commission (Art. 7(2), 14(4)) or the Secretariat (Art. 15(2), 19(4)). (4) Dismissal of experts is for the Commission (Art. 4(2), 13(4)) in some articles and for the AI Office (Art. 10(5)) in another. Entry into force is the twentieth day after OJ publication (Art. 20); the header shows issue date 10.3.2025, but the text states no entry-into-force date. Relation target_instrument_id is empty because no registry IDs were supplied.
